questions.prompt: The river completes a heart flush. You have Ah and no pair, no heart besides the ace. Against one thinking opponent…

choices.text: This is a possible bluff. You block the nut flush.
This is the nut flush already
You must fold without betting because an ace cannot bluff

questions.explanation: One heart in your hand is not a flush. The ace removes the best calling hand.

questions.prompt: Same completed flush, you have 72 with no heart against a station. Best default?

choices.text: Check. You do not block the nuts and they will not fold.

questions.explanation: No blocker and no fold equity is a give-up.

questions.prompt: You missed a draw and the river is a blank. The opponent has called two streets from a tight range. A bluff…

choices.text: Is usually a give-up. Their range is strong and the card did not scare them.
Works because blanks scare tight players
Should be an overbet with bottom pair

questions.explanation: Scare cards and blockers create bluffs. A blank against a strong caller does not.

questions.prompt: Which hand should not be turned into a bluff?

choices.text: A medium pair that beats some worse hands and loses to a raise.
Ace-high that blocks the nuts and loses to any call
A missed draw with the nut blocker

questions.explanation: Medium pairs are bluff-catchers or thin value, not bluffs. Betting them as a bluff folds out worse and gets called by better.
